statement: You are given an array nums sorted in non-decreasing order (it may contain duplicates) and an integer target.
The upper bound of target is the smallest index i such that nums[i] > target, strictly greater. Every copy of target is therefore skipped: the upper bound points just past the last one.
Return the upper bound. If no element is greater than target, the answer is n, the length of the array. Use binary search, so the work is O(log n).

examples.explanation: Indices 1 to 3 hold 2, which is not strictly greater than the target. nums[4] = 3 is the first element above 2, so the upper bound is 4.
3, 5 and 8 are all at most 9. nums[3] = 15 is the first element greater than 9, so the answer is 3.
